title: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse
sourceTitle: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse
synopsis: Your scout troop's overnight camp goes badly when, somehow, half of town becomes flesh-eating. You have a sash, three badges, and a slingshot. Use them.

nodes.text: Saturday morning. Troop leader is missing. Cocoa is cold. You and Carter and Augie find a zombie behind the storage shed.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Scream.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Tactical.

nodes.text: Carter wants to drive to the police station. The police station is, by Augie's count, two miles.

choices.consequence: Slow but safe.
You commit to “Bike.” The story records the instinct as “Faster” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Augie has, on his sash, a 'fire-making' badge, a 'first aid' badge, and a 'parade marshal' badge. The last one is, in fact, weirdly useful.

choices.consequence: Be the leader.
There is no taking “Mock the sash gently” back. Tone shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A woman named Denise appears with a baseball bat and saves you from a small mob. She is, immediately, in charge.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Smart.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Slow—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: The hardware store has nails, baseball bats, and a single guy named Ron behind the counter who has, apparently, been waiting for this.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Recruit Ron” back. More hands shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Take supplies and go.” The story records the instinct as “Speed” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: The mall, of course. Inside is a stage being set up for the high school party tonight. The party may still be on. Half the senior class doesn't know yet.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Warn the party” back. Save lives shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Defend.

nodes.text: The retirement home is, surprisingly, mostly fine. The residents have, for various reasons, mistaken the apocalypse for a fire drill.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Care—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Move on.

nodes.text: Kendall, Carter's crush, calls his phone. She is at the party. She is, somehow, alive. She is, also, smarter than Carter has ever realized.

choices.consequence: Crush as motive.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discipline.

nodes.text: A zombie cat. You both want to laugh and don't.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Soft.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Pragmatic—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: The school is locked. The football coach is, weirdly, leading a militia inside. He is, weirdly, doing it well.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Numbers.
You commit to “Avoid the militia.” The story records the instinct as “Loner” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You have, the badge book says, eighteen inches at minimum for accuracy. You discover, in practice, more like twelve.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discipline.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Battle test—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Augie, who has been the dorkiest of you for nine years, makes a move that saves Denise. The moment is small. The moment is huge.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Make sure he knows.” The story records the instinct as “Tell him” and carries it forward.
Some bravery is private.

nodes.text: An above-ground pool, a trampoline, two suburban kids' inheritance. You and Carter use them to clear a fence.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Catch up to Denise.” The story records the instinct as “Reconvene” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Friend first.

nodes.text: The mall stage is up. Half the high school is there. Music is loud. Nobody has noticed the zombies in the food court yet.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Cut the music” back. Get attention shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Lock the doors first” back. Contain shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Kendall, faced with the situation, organizes the party into a defense in under two minutes. You realize you have wildly underestimated her.

choices.consequence: “Follow her lead” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Smart.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Pair up.

nodes.text: The coach's militia arrives, late, but timely. Their plan is bad. Your plan is also bad. Together the plans become acceptable.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Merge the plans” back. Pragmatic shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
“Stay separate” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Discipline.

nodes.text: You orchestrate, against all reason, a trampoline-based charge that picks off the perimeter zombies in a way that, in a different timeline, would have been a YouTube video.

choices.consequence: Funny is fine.
There is no taking “Cover for it tactically” back. Discipline shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Augie's parade marshal badge actually saves the entire defensive arrangement by organizing them in a pattern only he knows. Augie, you realize, is the hero of this movie.

choices.consequence: “Promote Augie publicly” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Style.

nodes.text: Final wave. The football field. The stadium lights are on. You and Carter and Augie and Denise hold the south corner. Kendall holds the north.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Charge” back. Brave shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Patient.

nodes.text: Sunrise. The town is, mostly, scoured. The bus carrying the surviving teenagers pulls away. You and Augie sit on the bleachers eating, somehow, leftover pancakes.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—You won—follows you into whatever comes next.
“Sit quietly” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Decompress.

nodes.text: Monday morning. School is, weirdly, in session. The town has decided to call this a 'fire' for insurance reasons.

choices.consequence: “Stay scouts” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Sash on.
There is no taking “Quit scouts to be normal” back. Sash off shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You stay in scouts. You become an Eagle Scout. You write your application essay about the night the trampoline saved a high school. The reviewer, who has heard everything, says it is the most specific essay he has read.
Carter and Kendall become a couple. Augie, somehow, becomes the most popular kid at school. You become the friend who knows. You go on to a normal life that, every Halloween, gets weirder.
You quietly graduate. You never tell most people the truth about that night. You keep the sash in a box in your closet. Sometimes, late, you take it out and put it on. It still fits.
